findings.title: The Lord's response touches a world-encompassing scope
findings.claim: The supplied Fātiḥa phrase `رَبِّ ... عَٰلَمِينَ` widens the focus's personal `رَبُّهُ` and final `ٱلْعَلِيمُ` into a world-encompassing scope: Joseph's answered petition remains personal while the named Lord and knowledge touch the created whole.
findings.mechanism: The external occurrence `1:2:3` for `رَبِّ` and `1:2:4` for `عَٰلَمِينَ` makes direct contact with the focus occurrences `12:34:3:1` and `12:34:10:2`; the accepted focus lordship and world-creation facets therefore add scope beyond the native pericope without importing the whole external surah.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the response to Joseph as personal in address and broad in the scope attributed to the responding Lord and knowing-name.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay only. It does not translate `رَبُّهُ` as `رَبِّ ... عَٰلَمِينَ`, turn `ٱلْعَلِيمُ` into the noun for worlds, or apply the remaining Fātiḥa ayat without a local contact.

epistemic.reason: The external ayah and focus surface are supplied, while the widened scope is an inference from their direct repeated-root contacts and accepted focus branches.
